text.p: Bahrain on Sunday ordered the release of some prisoners, including people held in connection with anti-government protests, under a pardon ahead of the Gulf Arab state's silver jubilee, a government official said.

"The Emir (Sheikh Isa bin Sulman al-Khalifa) issued a decree pardoning tens of prisoners and some detainees who were held for security reasons to mark Bahrain's national day," the official told Reuters. He declined to give an exact figure.
Bahrain celebrates 25 years of independence on Monday.

Hundreds of people had been detained in connection with waves of violence, arson attacks and protests by members of the island's majority Shi'ite Moslem community seeking political and economic reforms.
